text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- GOVERNMENT WANTS SMALL FIRMS TO EXPORT

Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry over the next two years will make an effort to encourage small and medium-sized companies to export and raise the number of export firms to 80,000 from the current 15,000.
Brazilian shares rose sharply on Friday boosted by strong capital flows. The Sao Paulo bolsa ended up 2.04 percent on a surprising volume of 1.05 billion reais.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has benefitted from weak political parties and opposition, says Latin American professor Thomas Skidmore.
-- KUERTEN FIRST BRAZILIAN FRENCH OPEN CHAMP
Brazilian tennis player Gustavo Kuerten, 20, won the French Open, becoming the first Brazilian to win a grand slam tournament. Kuerten beat Spain's Sergi Bruguera 3-0 in one hour and fifty minutes.
Former U.S. tennis player John McEnroe said in New York Gustavo Kuerten "came to stay." McEnroe said Kuerten is a mixture of Brazilian soccer player Pele and U.S. soccer player Alexi Lalas.
-- BRAZIL TIES ITALY 3-3, GIVES ENGLAND THE TITLE
Brazil and Italy draw 3-3 in Lyon, giving England the Tournoi de France title.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
